skill.name: writing-bots
skill.description: Guides creation, testing, and operation of Silverback blockchain bots that react to blocks, contract events, cron jobs, and metrics.
skill.summary: Build Silverback bots for event-driven blockchain automation with testing and risk controls.
skill.author: ApeWorX

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives from inline documentation terms and code fences. The confirmed concerns are Silverback installation and run commands, environment-variable configuration, and autonomous blockchain transaction capability. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill includes commands to install and run Silverback tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running uv tool install or silverback run. Pin or verify Silverback versions when possible.

remediation.issue: Generated bots may sign and broadcast blockchain transactions.
remediation.suggestion: Default generated examples to read-only or dry-run behavior. Add spending limits, signer checks, staged testing, and circuit breakers before enabling transaction submission.

remediation.issue: Environment variables may contain sensitive configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Read only named variables, document required values, and avoid printing or sending environment values to logs or external services.

content.value_statement: Blockchain event bots need current SDK guidance and careful risk controls. This skill helps create Silverback bots with handlers, metrics, state, testing, and run steps.
actual_capabilities: Directs the assistant to fetch current Silverback documentation before writing bot code.
Guides handler design for new blocks, event logs, cron jobs, and metrics.
Explains when to maintain internal state and when to rely on on-chain state.
Suggests risk controls with environment variables, signer checks, and circuit breakers.
Provides setup and run guidance for uv and the Silverback CLI.
limitations: Requires uv and Silverback tooling for local execution.
Depends on external ApeWorX documentation for current API details.
Does not include a complete reusable bot template.
Generated bots still need review before signer or channel access.

use_cases.title: Monitor Contract Events
use_cases.description: Create a bot that reacts when a smart contract emits selected events on a target network.

use_cases.title: Run Operational Alerts
use_cases.description: Design bots that send messages, metrics, or service calls when blockchain conditions change.

use_cases.title: Prototype Transaction Automation
use_cases.description: Plan staged testing for bots that may later use a signer to submit controlled transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Describe a Simple Bot
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one event source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Silverback bot that watches one contract event on ethereum:mainnet. Ask for missing contract and event details first.

prompt_templates.title: Create Handler Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate bot outline with handlers and metrics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Silverback bot structure for new blocks, one event log, and a metric. Include where state should be avoided or used.

prompt_templates.title: Add Safety Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Silverback bot plan for operational risk. Add dry-run mode, configurable limits, signer checks, and circuit breaker conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Live Testing Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced staged rollout for a production-like bot.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged test plan for a Silverback bot that may broadcast transactions. Include logs, monitoring, rollback triggers, and approval gates.

output_examples.input: Design a bot that watches pool volume and alerts the team when volume crosses a threshold.
output_examples.output: A handler plan that uses a metric for pool volume, a threshold check, an alert action, and staged testing before production use.

output_examples.input: Review a bot before adding a signer.
output_examples.output: A safety checklist covering dry-run behavior, signer presence, balance checks, environment limits, logs, and circuit breaker triggers.

output_examples.input: Explain how to run the bot locally after review.
output_examples.output: A short run sequence that installs Silverback, selects the target network, starts the CLI, and monitors logs during testing.

best_practices: Fetch current Silverback documentation before writing or changing bot code.
Start with read-only behavior, logs, and metrics before enabling signers or external actions.
Use explicit limits, monitored rollout steps, and circuit breakers for every live bot.
anti_patterns: Do not give a new bot signer access before staged testing and user approval.
Do not rely on stale Silverback API knowledge when current documentation is available.
Do not print secrets, private keys, or raw environment values in logs.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design and write Silverback bots that react to blockchain events, metrics, cron jobs, and new blocks.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to fetch current ApeWorX Silverback documentation before writing code.

faq.question: Can it create bots that send transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses bots that may sign and broadcast transactions, so signer access needs strict review and limits.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it a full application template?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance for planning, writing, testing, and running a Silverback bot.

faq.question: What should users verify before running a bot?
faq.answer: Users should verify network choice, signer status, limits, logs, alert channels, and circuit breaker behavior.
